Subject: Post-call: Model fit + quantization trade study + POC next steps

Hi Morgan / Anika — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our side: 

Summary of needs you emphasized:
- Clinical summarization of patient encounter notes (long context, sensitive PHI handling)
- High throughput for near-real-time assistant (target p95 latency < 400ms for 512-token generates)
- Tight quality bar for factuality and hallucination (especially medication lists)

Initial model recommendations (based on today's workload description):
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (AWQ 4-bit): best cost/throughput trade for shorter turn-based summarization
- Llama-2-13b-chat (GPTQ 4-bit): higher baseline quality, recommended for long-context summarization tests
- Falcon-40B-Instruct (FP8 candidate): for final quality benchmark if you need best-in-class accuracy and can accept higher infra cost

Attachments I uploaded for your review: throughput_benchmarks.csv, prompt_set_v1.json, awq_gptq_tradeoff.pdf — these contain the microbenchmarks and a short trade study comparing AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 on accuracy/latency and cost. Link to a lightweight dashboard is below.

Next steps I'd like to propose:
1) POC scope: 2-week eval across Mistral-7B and Llama-2-13b-chat using your prompt set (we can iterate prompts).
2) Redwood will run two quantization profiles: AWQ 4-bit (aggressive quant) and GPTQ 4-bit (conservative), plus one FP8 run for Llama-2-13b-chat.
3) Deliverables: latency/throughput CSV, token-level cost estimate, top-3 failure cases per model, and an eval sheet with rubric for hallucinations and medical accuracy.
4) Technical kickoff: Wed 2026-03-04 10:00 PT — confirm if that works for your team.

Let me know if you'd prefer we scope a narrower pilot first. Thanks again — Marissa

--

Morgan — quick answers inline and attachments referenced below.

1) Quality delta (short answer): expect AWQ to be ~1–3% worse on our medical-fact precision metric vs GPTQ for the same base model, but AWQ often buys 1.8–2.5x throughput. FP8 is usually within 0–1% of fp16 quality but at much higher memory/serving cost. Details in awq_gptq_tradeoff.pdf and the Benchmarks link.

2) Neha — can you drop the SOC2/data-retention blurb here?

3) Cost target: for Mistral-7B with AWQ 4-bit during our internal runs we hit ~$0.018–0.025 per 1k generated tokens (assuming batching and KV caching tuned for your traffic). We'll include exact per-route cost estimates in the POC deliverable.

Attachments: throughput_benchmarks.csv (per-model latencies at 512/1024 tokens), prompt_set_v1.json (your initial prompt set with clinician examples), awq_gptq_tradeoff.pdf

If that looks OK I'll calendar the kickoff and include a short technical agenda.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit + quantization trade study + POC next steps

Hey team — technical note from infra/serving side (short):

- AWQ (our tuned variant) reduces matrix precision aggressively which improves cache utilization and reduces memory bandwidth. Practically: we observed 1.9–2.3x increase in tokens/sec versus GPTQ on A100-style hosts with similar batching.
- Quality-wise: on our clinical eval suite (the one in prompt_set_v1.json), AWQ shows a modest drop in span-level F1 for medication extraction (~2.2% absolute) compared to GPTQ; hallucination rates increased slightly in edge cases (long enumerations).
- GPTQ 4-bit is a safer default if you cannot tolerate any drop on med extraction; AWQ is recommended when throughput/cost is the gating factor and you can tolerate small targeted manual checks or augment with rule-based post-processing for meds.
- FP8: recommended for the final pass and stress-test; memory footprint goes up, and you'll likely need dedicated nodes (higher infra cost).

Proposal for POC testing matrix (we'll run these in parallel):
A) Mistral-7B: AWQ-4, GPTQ-4
B) Llama-2-13b-chat: GPTQ-4, FP8 (fp8 only for final accuracy run)

Metrics to capture: p50/p95 latency (512/1024 inputs), tokens/sec, token cost estimate, span-F1 for meds, hallucination count per 1k summaries, top-10 failure examples.

I'll put a lightweight runbook in the Drive folder before kickoff. Happy to be the technical owner for run execution.

-Dylan

Morgan — brief SOC2/data retention note for your legal team: 
- Redwood stores POC logs for 30 days by default. Logs can be disabled per-route for PHI-sensitive traffic; we recommend sending redacted samples or using a private deployment if you want zero retention.
- We support customer-managed keys (KMS) and VPC-only Private deployments for production; POC runs can use encrypted channels and we will enable log redaction/disable on request.
- I'll drop a one-pager to the Drive folder (SOC2_POc_summary.pdf) and share it with your legal inbox after you confirm NDA.

Also — happy to coordinate the NDA handoff. If Quantify can sign a standard Redwood POC addendum we can start with deidentified samples within 24 hrs.

Neha Kapoor
